ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in Figure A, the turn ratio of the primary and secondary coils of the ideal transformer is 10∶11, and L is a coil with a relatively large self-inductance coefficient. When the alternating voltage shown in Figure B is applied to both ends of the primary coil of the transformer, the light bulb glows normally. Which of the following statements is correct? (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure A, the turn ratio of the primary and secondary coils of the ideal transformer is 10∶11, and L is a coil with a relatively large self-inductance coefficient. When the alternating voltage shown in Figure B is applied to both ends of the primary coil of the transformer, what is the instantaneous value expression of the voltage shown in Figure B?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: On the left side of Figure A is an ideal transformer and a circuit connected externally to its secondary coil, containing a light bulb D, self-inductance coil L, and sliding rheostat P, indicating that the alternating voltage shown in Figure B is connected to both ends of the primary coil; for this question, the voltage-time graph in Figure B is mainly used. The vertical axis of Figure B is labeled u/V, and the positive and negative peak values are respectively at +200 V and -200 V; the horizontal axis is labeled t/(×10^-2 s). The curve is a sine curve, starting from t=0, u=0 and increasing in the positive direction, indicating that the initial phase is 0. Adjacent points with the same phase are separated by 2 horizontal-axis units, so the period T=2×10^-2 s. Then reason: The instantaneous value of sinusoidal alternating current can be written as u=Um sin(ωt+φ). From the graph, Um=200 V and φ=0; the angular frequency ω=2π/T=2π/(2×10^-2)=100π rad/s. Substituting gives the instantaneous value expression of the voltage shown in Figure B as u=200 sin(100πt) V.
